This notebook is a small, data-backed smoke-check for GB processing. It reads the
current GB export and configuration, applies name exclusions and the configured
sample peak-number range, applies a diagnostic linear drift correction using
ETH4, and compares raw and drift-adjusted standard values. It does not apply an
intensity or scale correction or save processed results.

```{r setup}
library(isotidy)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

data_path <- file.path(
  "..",
  "..",
  "data",
  "20260826_tp_DIC_GB-IRMS"
)

config_path <- file.path(
  data_path,
  "analyzed_data",
  "experiment_config.yaml"
)

lab_config_dir <- file.path(
  "..",
  "..",
  "..",
  "sessions_lab_isotidy_config"
)

config <- load_IRMS_config(config_path, lab_config_dir)

raw_data_path <- file.path(
  data_path,
  "raw_data",
  paste0(config$file_name, ".xls")
)

raw_gb <- readxl::read_xls(raw_data_path)

schemas <- load_peripheral_schemas()
schema <- get_peripheral_schema(
  schemas = schemas,
  peripheral = "GB"
)
```

## Process the export

Review this inventory to identify the analyses from the second day. Enter their
`Analysis` values in `exclude_analysis_numbers` below; the processor will remove
all peaks belonging to those analyses and report them in `excluded_analyses`.

```{r analysis-inventory}
format_gb_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) return(format(as.Date(x), "%Y-%m-%d"))
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) return(format(x, "%Y-%m-%d"))
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(format(as.Date(x, origin = "1899-12-30"), "%Y-%m-%d"))
  trimws(as.character(x))
}

format_gb_time <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) return(format(x, "%H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))
  if (inherits(x, "hms")) x <- as.numeric(x)
  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    seconds <- ifelse(abs(x) < 1, x * 86400, x %% 86400)
    return(format(
      as.POSIXct(round(seconds), origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
      "%H:%M:%S",
      tz = "UTC"
    ))
  }
  trimws(as.character(x))
}

parse_gb_datetime <- function(date_text, time_text) {
  datetime_text <- paste(date_text, time_text)
  formats <- c(
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M",
    "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S", "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M",
    "%m/%d/%y %H:%M:%S", "%m/%d/%y %H:%M"
  )
  parsed <- as.POSIXct(rep(NA_real_, length(datetime_text)),
                       origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
  for (date_format in formats) {
    candidate <- as.POSIXct(datetime_text, format = date_format, tz = "UTC")
    use_candidate <- is.na(parsed) & !is.na(candidate)
    parsed[use_candidate] <- candidate[use_candidate]
  }
  parsed
}

raw_analysis_inventory <- raw_gb |>
  group_by(
    analysis_no = .data[["Analysis"]],
    raw_sample_id = .data[["Identifier 1"]],
    analysis_date = .data[["Date"]],
    analysis_time = .data[["Time"]]
  ) |>
  summarise(n_exported_peaks = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
mutate(
    date_text = format_gb_date(analysis_date),
    time_text = format_gb_time(analysis_time)
  )

raw_analysis_inventory <- raw_analysis_inventory |>
  mutate(analysis_datetime = parse_gb_datetime(date_text, time_text))

if (anyNA(raw_analysis_inventory$analysis_datetime)) {
  stop("Some GB analysis date/time values could not be parsed; inspect the inventory.")
}

raw_analysis_inventory <- raw_analysis_inventory |>
  arrange(analysis_date, analysis_datetime, analysis_no) |>
  group_by(analysis_date) |>
  mutate(
    run_analysis_number = row_number(),
    elapsed_minutes = as.numeric(
      difftime(analysis_datetime, min(analysis_datetime), units = "mins")
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

raw_analysis_inventory
```

```{r adapt}
# Replace these with the Analysis numbers for the later-day standards.
exclude_analysis_numbers <- c(65135, 65136, 65138, 65139, 65140)

gb_result <- process_gb(
  raw_df = raw_gb,
  config = config,
  schema = schema,
  isotope = "C13",
  run_id = config$file_name,
  exclude_analysis_numbers = exclude_analysis_numbers,
  drift_standard_id = "ETH4",
  apply_drift_correction = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

gb_data <- gb_result$data
```

Configured sample peak numbers are shown below. All name-filtered peaks remain
available as `gb_result$all_peak_data`; peaks outside the sample range are in
`gb_result$excluded_peaks`. Analyses excluded by number are available in
`gb_result$excluded_analyses`.

```{r configured-range}
gb_result$sample_peak_numbers
nrow(gb_result$data)
nrow(gb_result$excluded_peaks)
nrow(gb_result$excluded_analyses)
gb_result$drift_correction[c(
  "applied", "reason", "standard_id", "n_standard_analyses",
  "analysis_range", "reference_delta", "slope_per_analysis",
  "r_squared", "slope_p_value", "residual_sd",
  "extrapolated_rows"
)]
gb_result$drift_correction$standard_analyses
```

## Explore NaHCO3 isotope value versus intensity

The standard concentration is retained in `standard_variant` (for example,
`_1umol`). The plot shows every selected peak, colored by the original label so
the concentration series is visible. The regression below uses one mean point
per injection, avoiding treating the multiple peaks from one injection as
independent standard injections.

```{r nahco3-intensity-data}
nahco3_peaks <- gb_data |>
  filter(standard_id == "NaHCO3") |>
  filter(
    is.finite(delta_value),
    is.finite(area_or_voltage),
    area_or_voltage > 0
  ) |>
  mutate(
    concentration_label = if_else(
      is.na(standard_variant) | standard_variant == "",
      "(no concentration suffix)",
      standard_variant
    )
  )

nahco3_injections <- nahco3_peaks |>
  group_by(injection_id, raw_sample_id, concentration_label) |>
  summarise(
    n_peaks = n(),
    mean_delta = mean(delta_value),
    mean_delta_raw = mean(delta_value_raw),
    mean_area = mean(area_or_voltage),
    sd_delta = sd(delta_value),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(mean_delta), is.finite(mean_area), mean_area > 0)

stopifnot(
  nrow(nahco3_peaks) > 0,
  nrow(nahco3_injections) > 2,
  dplyr::n_distinct(nahco3_injections$concentration_label) > 1,
  dplyr::n_distinct(nahco3_injections$mean_area) > 1
)

nahco3_concentration_summary <- nahco3_injections |>
  count(concentration_label, name = "n_injections") |>
  arrange(concentration_label)

nahco3_concentration_summary
```

```{r nahco3-intensity-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(
  nahco3_peaks,
  aes(x = area_or_voltage, y = delta_value, color = concentration_label)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "NaHCO3: isotope value versus peak intensity",
    x = "Area / voltage (log10 scale)",
    y = expression(delta^{13}*"C (‰)"),
    color = "Standard label"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Fit a linear relationship between isotope value and log intensity using the
injection means. The slope is in delta units per tenfold increase in area. Its
p-value is exploratory; concentration and injection effects may still be
confounded, and the peak-level plot should be reviewed alongside the fit.

```{r nahco3-intensity-fit}
nahco3_fit <- lm(mean_delta ~ log10(mean_area), data = nahco3_injections)
nahco3_fit_summary <- summary(nahco3_fit)
nahco3_fit_raw <- lm(mean_delta_raw ~ log10(mean_area), data = nahco3_injections)
nahco3_fit_raw_summary <- summary(nahco3_fit_raw)

data.frame(
  correction = c("uncorrected", "drift corrected"),
  n_injections = nrow(nahco3_injections),
  slope_per_log10_area = c(
    unname(coef(nahco3_fit_raw)[[2]]),
    unname(coef(nahco3_fit)[[2]])
  ),
  r_squared = c(nahco3_fit_raw_summary$r.squared, nahco3_fit_summary$r.squared),
  p_value_for_slope = c(
    nahco3_fit_raw_summary$coefficients[2, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    nahco3_fit_summary$coefficients[2, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  )
)
```

```{r nahco3-injection-fit-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(
  nahco3_injections,
  aes(x = mean_area, y = mean_delta, color = concentration_label)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, color = "black") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "NaHCO3 injection means and exploratory intensity fit",
    x = "Mean area / voltage (log10 scale)",
    y = expression("Mean "*delta^{13}*"C (‰)"),
    color = "Standard label"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Check for peak-order effects within each analysis

Here each line is one GB analysis (one vial/sample acquisition), and points are
the repeated loop-injection peaks from that analysis. These peaks are not
independent replicate analyses. The plots check whether the first included
peak differs systematically or whether isotope values drift across peak order.

```{r nahco3-peak-order-summary}
nahco3_peak_order_summary <- nahco3_peaks |>
  arrange(injection_id, peak_number) |>
  group_by(injection_id, raw_sample_id, concentration_label) |>
  summarise(
    n_peaks = n(),
    first_peak_number = first(peak_number),
    last_peak_number = last(peak_number),
    first_peak_delta = first(delta_value),
    later_mean_delta = if (n() > 1) mean(delta_value[-1]) else NA_real_,
    first_minus_later_delta = first_peak_delta - later_mean_delta,
    within_analysis_sd_delta = sd(delta_value),
    delta_change_first_to_last = last(delta_value) - first(delta_value),
    first_peak_area = first(area_or_voltage),
    later_mean_area = if (n() > 1) mean(area_or_voltage[-1]) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(first_minus_later_delta)))

stopifnot(
  nrow(nahco3_peak_order_summary) > 0,
  all(nahco3_peak_order_summary$n_peaks > 1),
  all(nahco3_peak_order_summary$last_peak_number >
        nahco3_peak_order_summary$first_peak_number)
)

nahco3_peak_order_summary
```

```{r nahco3-delta-by-peak-order, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ggplot(
  nahco3_peaks,
  aes(
    x = peak_number,
    y = delta_value,
    group = injection_id,
    color = concentration_label
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(vars(concentration_label), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(nahco3_peaks$peak_number))) +
  labs(
    title = "NaHCO3 isotope value by peak order within analysis",
    x = "Peak number",
    y = expression(delta^{13}*"C (‰)"),
    color = "Standard label"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r nahco3-area-by-peak-order, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ggplot(
  nahco3_peaks,
  aes(
    x = peak_number,
    y = area_or_voltage,
    group = injection_id,
    color = concentration_label
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(vars(concentration_label), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(nahco3_peaks$peak_number))) +
  labs(
    title = "NaHCO3 peak intensity by peak order within analysis",
    x = "Peak number",
    y = "Area / voltage",
    color = "Standard label"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Evaluate ETH4 across analysis order

ETH4 is used here as a repeated standard across the run. Each point below is
one analysis summarized across its configured sample peaks; the table retains
the within-analysis standard deviation and mean signal so run drift and
intensity changes can be inspected separately. Any analysis numbers entered
above are excluded from this evaluation too.

```{r eth4-analysis-summary}
eth4_analyses <- gb_data |>
  filter(standard_id == "ETH4") |>
  group_by(analysis_date, analysis_no) |>
  summarise(
    n_peaks = n(),
    mean_delta_raw = mean(delta_value_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_delta = mean(delta_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_delta_within_analysis = sd(delta_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_area = mean(area_or_voltage, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    raw_analysis_inventory |>
      select(
        analysis_date,
        analysis_no,
        analysis_datetime,
        run_analysis_number,
        elapsed_minutes
      ),
    by = c("analysis_date", "analysis_no")
  ) |>
  arrange(analysis_date, run_analysis_number)

stopifnot(
  nrow(eth4_analyses) > 2,
  dplyr::n_distinct(eth4_analyses$analysis_no) > 2,
  all(is.finite(eth4_analyses$mean_delta)),
  all(is.finite(eth4_analyses$mean_area)),
  all(is.finite(eth4_analyses$run_analysis_number)),
  all(is.finite(eth4_analyses$elapsed_minutes))
)

eth4_analyses
```

```{r eth4-drift-comparison-data}
eth4_delta_comparison <- bind_rows(
  eth4_analyses |>
    transmute(
      analysis_date,
      analysis_no,
      run_analysis_number,
      elapsed_minutes,
      mean_delta = mean_delta_raw,
      correction = "uncorrected"
    ),
  eth4_analyses |>
    transmute(
      analysis_date,
      analysis_no,
      run_analysis_number,
      elapsed_minutes,
      mean_delta,
      correction = "drift corrected"
    )
)
```

```{r eth4-isotope-by-analysis, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(
  eth4_delta_comparison,
  aes(
    x = run_analysis_number,
    y = mean_delta,
    color = correction,
    group = correction
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(analysis_date), scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("uncorrected" = "#D55E00", "drift corrected" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(
    title = "ETH4 mean isotope value before and after drift correction",
    x = "Run-specific analysis order (instrument Analysis ID is in the table)",
    y = expression("Mean "*delta^{13}*"C (‰)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r eth4-area-by-analysis, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(eth4_analyses, aes(x = run_analysis_number, y = mean_area)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "#287C8E") +
  facet_wrap(vars(analysis_date), scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "ETH4 mean intensity across analysis order",
    x = "Run-specific analysis order (instrument Analysis ID is in the table)",
    y = "Mean area / voltage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r eth4-isotope-by-elapsed-time, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(
  eth4_delta_comparison,
  aes(
    x = elapsed_minutes,
    y = mean_delta,
    color = correction,
    group = interaction(analysis_date, correction)
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(analysis_date), scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("uncorrected" = "#D55E00", "drift corrected" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(
    title = "ETH4 isotope value before and after drift correction",
    x = "Minutes since first analysis of that date",
    y = expression("Mean "*delta^{13}*"C (‰)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Drift correction is applied as a linear change in mean ETH4 isotope value per
instrument `Analysis` number, centered on the mean fitted ETH4 value. Compare
the raw and corrected curves and inspect the fitted standard table above;
ETH4 is the fitting reference, so its flattening is not an independent
validation. The NaHCO3 intensity slope table compares the candidate area trend
before and after drift adjustment. The separate within-analysis SD shows
whether repeated peaks themselves are stable.
